title: DR-DCI: Scaling Direct Corpus Interaction via Dynamic Workspace Expansion

visual_explainer.question: Can retrieval become an agent action that dynamically grows a persistent DCI workspace instead of fixing the evidence set up front?
visual_explainer.takeaway: DR-DCI alternates retriever-steered workspace expansion with local DCI operations, using retrieval for corpus-scale recall and direct interaction for evidence resolution.
visual_explainer.compared_with: Raw full-corpus DCI, static retrieved workspaces, and conventional top-k retrieval agents.

analysis.tldr: DR-DCI turns retrieval into an agent-callable pull operation that expands a persistent local workspace, then applies shell-style DCI inside that bounded state; global recall and local evidence interaction become separate control layers.
analysis.problem: Raw DCI is expressive but operationally unstable at large corpus scale, while fixed retrieval limits the agent to the ranking/view chosen before local evidence constraints emerge.
analysis.core_idea: Maintain a query-specific workspace. At any turn the agent can pull ranked documents with a chosen query/budget, inspect and compare all materialized documents through DCI tools, or finalize. Retrieved evidence persists across subsequent actions.
analysis.agent_loop: reason → pull(query,k) to expand workspace → inspect/compare with DCI → refine constraints → pull again or verify → answer
analysis.retrieval_design: Retrieval performs corpus-level candidate discovery; DCI performs workspace-level search, comparison, and span verification. A ranked preview guides attention without becoming the canonical evidence interface.
analysis.evidence: On the full 830-query BrowseComp-Plus evaluation, DR-DCI reports 71.20% accuracy versus 62.90% for Raw-DCI while reducing average tool calls from 37.53 to 30.94, wall time from 3139.10s to 146.16s, and estimated total cost from $88.13 to $34.91. Optional workspace-preserving context reset reaches 73.25%. Controlled scaling covers 100K–10M documents, and the interface also transfers to a 20M-document Wiki-18 setting.
analysis.why_it_matters: This is a strong systems answer to the DCI scaling problem: the environment is no longer either a fixed top-k result or the entire corpus. Retrieval itself becomes a state-changing workspace-management action.
limitations: The method bundles retrieval, workspace materialization, terminal-aware harness engineering, ranked previews, and optional context reset.
External reference systems are not fully controlled baselines; the strongest causal evidence is Raw-DCI and interface ablations under the shared harness.
Large-scale QA uses sampled evaluation splits and file-per-document corpora; open-web freshness and mutable sources remain outside scope.
